posts.title: Forum for posting comments on mixed methods and qualitative method (due Jan 12)

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Understanding Self-Report Bias in Organizational Behavior Research

This article is discussing about the bias that might occur when doing the organizational behavior research and when the researchers require the participants to do self-reporting. I can understand from the perspective of the participant that in the self-reporting method of study. I would always fill the thing that is acceptable by the society and create a great impression for the society. Hence, it is interesting to bring up this issue as a part of the study and by reading this article, I am more aware of the importance of doing variance method of study, such as using another set of data as comparison, is beneficial to reduce the potential of biasness, especially for the self-report method.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
1.    Self-report: how to question shape the answer

This article discusses about creating questions that are good for experiment is not an easy process. This makes me think that when the researchers are having difficulty of analyzing the data because the data appear to be undesirable and cause a lot of assumption and ambiguity involve. However, after reading this paper, I think that it might be due to the failure of framing the questions that is perceived well by the respondents. Back in my bachelor degree, I was having a simple project for one of my course to do the user survey about a system. However, after doing the research and gathering the information, the result of the analysis appears to be ambiguous and it produce not a good result. I remembered on that day as well, my professor also told my team that he found some ambiguity in my questionnaire that had caused the ambiguity to result to happen. Yet, on that time, I am kind of lost in how to make good questionnaire questions then? After I read this paper, I think this paper might be one of the guide and also can help to reflect more on how to frame a good questionnaires or self-reporting’s set of question that can help me to acquire the answer that I desire.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Understanding self-reported bias in organizational behavior research

It is a key issue that respondents with a propensity to socially desirable attitudes seek to report behavior in a more favorable manner than those lower on this dispositional characteristic. These results point out that self-report bias tends not to be uniform across constructs assessed in psychological research conducted in business settings. On this point, multiple data sources are needed to help rule out the validity threats of self-report and mono-method. Therefore, it reminds researchers that the importance of experiment design that may be able to isolate actual behavior and situational method effects.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
An Introduction to Codes and Coding

    This article is the first article I’ve read that gives a really comprehensive look of coding. I hence understand that the coding work that I did previously is just a kind of use of coding. We previously code for the keywords in a participants self-report to find their attitudes toward a service, while coding can also be done on the entire page of text, or a stream of moving images, and the use of codes can be to find certain pattern of actions in human affairs.
    The author says coding is not a precise science; it’s primarily an interpretive act, which relieve my worries during coding this job. As long as we understand what’s the goal of the job can choose the right filter(perspective) to look at your data, every one of us can have an interesting and meaningful code for the data, it is interesting isn’t it?

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Self-report: how to question shape the answer

    Wow, I knew that the way we design questionnaire will affect the answer we get. But I never knew the impact is that huge, and I didn’t expect such little difference(such as whether a list is provided, and the range of Likert scale) mentioned in the article would drastically influence the survey result. 
    Even the most intuitive thing, ask out a question, can influence participant’s responses due to different understanding of the question. When we want to take care of the question we ask, not only should we make sure the participants understand literal meaning of the wording, but also we have to let them get the right pragmatic meaning of the question, that is, the participants have to know which category of answer we are interested in.
    I should bare these suggestions in mind when conducting survey, and we should critic others surveys, are their questions understood by the respondents?

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Quantifying Qualitative Analyses of Verbal Data: A Practical Guide

I only read a part of this article, in my part, the author gives an introduction about Verbal Analysis Method. Verbal Analysis Method has been embedded in research about understanding mainly learner’s cognition. The way of conducting Verbal Analysis is to code explanations of what one understands as one reads a text sentence-by-sentence, to see whether an explanation is an inference, a monitoring statement, or some other irrelevant comment. The author also points out that there may be bias when we ''structure’’ the utterance, it is some times difficult for us to be certain if utterances are unrelated pieces of knowledge or they can be captured by a few principles or maybe the relation is more complicated.

This article is quite hard since it delve deep into a method which I have yet understand, I decide to gain more knowledge about Verbal Analysis Method before continuing reading this article.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Self-report: how to question shape the answer

The design of self-report questionnaire has a major impact on the answers. The author reviewed a lot of researches about the features of self-report questionnaire (e.g. the issues of question comprehension) and intended to tell us how features of the research instrument shape the answers, even influence the conclusions of a research.

One of that is rating scales. It reminded me that a question was mentioned in class about how to design a rating scale and which ranges of rating (from 0 to 5 vs. from -2 to 2) is better. The article gives a great answer to this question. The example from the article is the success-in-life question with an 11-point rating scale that ranged either from 0 (not at all successful) to 10 (extremely successful), or from -5 to 5. The results showed that the ratings respondents provided are strongly related to the means by “not at all successful”.

Because my research is about behavior change, the participants would be asked behavioral frequency reports. These self-reports are a primary source of data in my research. Fortunately, the article let me have ideas how to adjust the questionnaire.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
An Introduction to Codes and Coding

This first chapter was a very useful overview not just about the mechanics surrounding coding but also about general understanding and debated issues regarding it. It also introduced me to deeper terminology and methods for qualitative coding. For example, I was aware of the cyclical nature of coding in that it usually involves many iterations, but terms such as Descriptive Code vs In Vivo Code and others were new to me. They were useful to know even if I hadn't planned on using them immediately in my research but at least now I might better understand if asked questions about future qualitative codes. 

I also really appreciated the solid section delineating more meta approaches of pattern detection, in emphasizing that we should not forget to look for "super-patterns" not just from the single layer of codes generated - such as noticing idiosyncrasy (individualities or differences in common) and variation in patterns themselves.

A very important section to me was also about debated issues about what coding itself entails and related topics, and it is reasonable that this exists due to the inherent biased nature of coding. The introduction of various metaphors to help understand the state of coding and different perspectives on it were helpful, such as coding providing the bones for analysis and then integration assembling them into a working skeleton. I was previously unaware there were actually so many different well-known argued issues surrounding coding such as what constitutes a code, and the boundaries between coding and analysis. The difference between codes and themes was explained which is helpful, as the issue can be confusing - coding can involve keyword-based categorization of the data where some keywords can seem to translate into themes but may not actually be quite enough.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
An introduction to Codes and Coding

This article introduces and giving a guide about how to code the data that is originated from qualitative method of study. It has taught me a lot about how to do appropriate coding the qualitative data that I get from, such as, interview. I think the guide is very clear and clear. Also, it provides step-by-step instruction on how to work on coding the qualitative data. Also, it helps the reader, especially the beginner in the qualitative research, to understand and pay attention to the things that necessarily to be avoided. Lastly, what is good about this paper is it explains the concept coding by providing the examples on each important explanation. Hence, it will help the beginner or the new comer of qualitative researchers to prevent misunderstanding. Especially, when coding the qualitative data is harder due to its freedom, without any preset or structured rules or formula.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
An Introduction to Codes and Coding

Diverse methods and terminology for qualitative coding are introduced in the article. The topic is totally new to me. I have few experience with qualitative analysis. The concepts of codes and coding are clearly and concretely illustrated. For example, we should design context-based coding filters to fit our research's analytic lens. By doing so, we can retrieve compact and precise information from collected data. Furthermore, it is also important that we should record all data throughout experiment. If not, we only can get the "surface" when coding.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
A useful things to know about machine learning.

This article is useful for knowing more concept and understand the use of machine learning and also attributes that that are complementing it. Machine learning can help us to perform a task by generalizing the example and it is more cost-effective rather than do the manual coding one-by-one. Overall, there are a lot of things that need to be such as the classifier, the data and many more, to perform a reliable and accurate machine learning. Overall, I would recommend this paper to anyone who wants to get the surface level of understanding of machine learning. At least, this article is good for highlighting some key items that promote good and reliable machine learning

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
UNDERSTANDING SELF-REPORT BIAS IN ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR RESEARCH

I view this paper as related to the previous article I read — “Self-report: how to question shape the answer”. I the previous article, they discuss how the way we ask out the question would affect the answer of participants. In this paper, the authors point out another potential self-report bias. That is even you’ve ask the right question and even the respondents fully understand the question, there is still sometimes you can get a faulty result due to the respondents’ propensity to give accurate answer to some questions. 

This issue is analyzed in the paper and they found some measures are likely to be misleading, for example some measures of performance and mental health. The research also suggest that using multiple sources of data(multiple methods of deriving data) is a desirable way to avoid serious bias.

While this paper shed lights mainly on business settings, I believe all the researchers should take this seriously since the misleading results may lead to wrong conclusion and threaten not only the paper’s value but people’s understanding of the research topic.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Self-report: how to question shape the answer

Author put together lots of research and focus on the problems that may happened when design a good self-repots questionnaire. Some question may confuse subjects; some subjects may misunderstand the questions. It seems was an unsolvable problems, but we could decrease the probability of such mistakes by design right questions. It made me recall that I had the experience about feel troubled about the questionnaire when I was a senior student. My friends and I think it was our problem that we could not understand what part of those questions means at that time, now I realize it was not all our fault. To improve such understanding problem, there was another solution which is change the self-repots questionnaire type from word to non-verbal pictorial just like Lang(1985).
Another interesting thing about design questionnaire is the option we provide to subjects. Author illustrated some examples at the beginning of the article. I think this is the part that should be pay attention to research. Because the prior part, that is the design of right question, may be easier to solve by just asking friends around us, but the latter part, is more difficult to discover in advance and always need us to really collect the data or learn from the experience of others.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Self-report : How the Questions Shape the Answers

In the field of psychology and social science, users' self-reports give the primary source of data. Most basically, the survey/questionnaire collects the users' opinions for researcher to learn and analyze users' thoughts and behaviors. This article gave us a guideline and basic principle of forming reasonable questions, since the wording, question format and context might result in big difference of the responses.

I did know that the wording of questions is important, but it is more ideal to form comprehensive questions, since it help respondent get into the scenario and also help them better recall the memory when they are facing such situation in real life. Also, the scale matters a lot. It's important to reduce the bias, not to say the one caused by researchers themselves.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Understanding self-report bias in organizational behavior research 

Self-report bias occurs when research participants tend to under-report behaviors deemed inappropriate by researchers or other observers, and they tend to over-report behaviors viewed as appropriate.

 

We can’t absolutely avoid the bias, but we can decrease the bias. There may be some bias in my current research when we assign participants to record their daily traveling. To decrease the bias, we use a wearable camera being a comparison to check up the validity of the data. Furthermore, we provide an advanced method which is combines with two traditional methods to increase the accuracy. We hypothesize that this new method improves both self-report bias and accuracy.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
An Introduction to Codes and Coding 

This manual focuses on codes and coding and how they play a role in the qualitative data analytic process. The most impressive part is introduction of Codifying and Categorizing. To codify is to arrange things in a systematic order, to make something part of a system or classification, to categorize. Since I learn some classification and clustering method this semester, I am very interested in categorizing. The manual uses a streamlined codes-to-theory model for qualitative inquiry diagram to illustrate   a very basic process, codifying usually follows an ideal and streamlined scheme. We can see the process from particular code to general theory. And in the following section there are also more detailed explanation for each hierarchy of the streamline. After reading this manual, I can have more knowledge when doing qualitative research.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Designing HCI experiments

The process of designing an experiment is one of enhancing the signal while reducing the noise. One crucial step that precedes the design of every HCI experiment is ethics approval, so I have gone to IRB course which is relative to ethics research for human behavioral. Other parts in this paper is likely to the content professor taught in class, such as dependent/independent variable, other variables, within/between subject design, counterbalancing and so on. They explain more deeply and give some examples to help readers be clearer about the experiment design. When the experiment is designed, the apparatus built and tested, the participants recruited and scheduled, then testing almost begins. However, a pilot should be implemented before researchers begin experiment. This will help researchers find out some problems that didn’t notice when designing the experiment. Due to the introduction in the paper, I have more concepts about designing HCI experiment and understand something I mistaken in the previous study design homework.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Self-reports: How the questions shape the answers

“Is the question make sense?” which is always asked to us by professor. The key issue is whether the respondents’ understanding of the question matches what the researchers had in mind. However, when it comes to response, there are open and close response formats. Suppose that respondents are asked in an open-response format, they will try to determine which activities may be of interest to the researcher. Someone is likely to omit activities that the researcher is obviously aware of or may take for granted anyway. Nevertheless, if they are given a list of activities that included what they did, most respondents would endorse them. At the same time, such a list would reduce the likelihood that respondents would report activities that are not represented on the list.

In my current study, to avoid the problem above, we use a method called annotation, giving columns for participants to annotate more accurately information that doesn’t include in ESM. So that would be open and close response format in the meantime.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
UNDERSTANDING SELF-REPORT BIAS IN ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR RESEARCH

This article can be connecting with “Self-report: how to question shape the answer”. Prior one I read talked about the design of questionnaire. Problems seem to come from researchers and I also share my comments stood in research’s shoes. And this one is about the under-report and over-report behavior occurs when participants concern about others opinion, focus on organizational behavior research. Problems can be considered from participants. There is another reason that participants under-report or over-report behaviors. In my experience in collect questionnaire data, I have heard a participant mumbled “I remember researchers always do not like the neutral answer”, in order to help researchers, participant choice to under-report the scale. Such problems cannot be easy solved by the design of questionnaire. But just like author suggest, maybe we could use multiple methods to collect data to decrease the bias.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
An Introduction to Codes and Coding

Categorizing has been an interesting thing to me since I took data mining course, and coding is a method that enables us to organize and group similarly coded data into categories. Therefore, this guide is absorbing to me, and also inspiring. Actually categorizing is a usual process for people in everyday life, by systematically realizing coding, I know more clearly about the rules and methods when we classify in the brain. Some terms like Descriptive Code, In Vivo Code, Initial Coding, Process Code, and Simultaneous Coding also help me code the qualitative data efficiently and appropriately. I think most important thing we should note is “you think of patterns not just as stable regularities but as varying forms” and “A pattern can be characterized by similarity, difference, frequency, sequence, correspondence and causation”. By recalling those characteristic, we can find pattern in more easy way.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
Self-report: How the Questions Shape the Answers

This article discusses how questions presentation influence participants answers when doing self-report and suggests some tips to improve questionnaire design. Learning from previous research, minor changes in questions (e.g., wording, rating scale, provided examples) can significantly influence the results. It is mainly due to answerers may inferring different intention of the questioner from different represented questions.

Though I knew that self-report answers are not reliable, and what they say may differ from what they really is. This reading shows another perspective from conversational point of view, saying that pragmatic meaning of a question should be well transferred. Though I learn much about what we should prevent from, I still found it hard to make clear, informative, and quality question, and the pretest procedure is also challenging.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
UNDERSTANDING SELF-REPORT BIAS IN ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR RESEARCH

This reading discuss the bias of using self-report method in organizational behavior research. Self-report bias in organizational behavior research mainly comes from participants intention to respond in socially desirable ways. They conducted archival research on a large-scale dataset. Their result implies importance of triangulation research method for avoiding bias in result.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Self-reports: How the questions shape the answers

The reading is really helpful to make me think my questionnaire design again. Actually it is very hard for participants to tell themselves what experience is during testing. We need to design a suit of questions to guide them to explore actual thoughts. The reading illustrates the fact that questions presentations will affect the answers we get from different aspects, such as the range of rating scale and wording. I should keep my mind on those suggestions when designing questionnaire in the future.
